featured_reviews.name: Parv Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a terrible experience watching Project Hail Mary in Screen 2 of this theater.

Seats are comfortable, but the hall had a sweaty smell, it was probably the AC/ventilation not working properly.

The film started playing with the lights turned ON inside the hall. It was only after 5-10 minutes into the film that the lights were turned off. And then the film was restarted.

Since Project Hail Mary has multiple aspect ratios you can expect pillarboxing (black sides) coming and going as the scenes change during the film. But what you don't want is an uncalibrated projector scaling on the screen - a small gap in the top and bottom of the screen, which never goes away because the projector is not set up properly.

Speaking of which, the image rendering is good, I could see the grains too, but the focus was just a bit off. Moreover, the screen was dirty in the center right with a huge mark. Looked like someone tried to clean but accidentally smeared. It blackened the projection in that spot.

The audio was average, but the center channel had a constant loud buzzing. Which was a major distraction in the experience of the film.

Overall it felt like watching a pirated copy of the film in some second-hand theater setup. Definitely not satisfactory or worth the time. The ticket prices were INR 91/- so I felt like they deliberately choose the worse performing screen (Screen 2).

I believe that Miraj Cinemas can do so much better. Not everyone wants to watch Dhurandhar, so please take good care of ALL of your customers.

Audio: 4/10
Video: 5/10
Ticket price: Rs. 91 (the experience shouldn't reflect that)

review_photos.caption: Notice the big dark patch on the right of "Sony Pictures" text. It looked darker in reality. When the screen was not playing anything, you could see it very clearly.
Notice the top and bottom gap. It is not intentional. The film only changed the ratio horizontally. So the gap remained there nontheless.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointed with the Staff's Arrogant Behaviour!
​Visited Miraj Cinemas, Mulund today for a 9:15 PM show. I reached the entry gate around 8:40 PM. Instead of being polite, the female security guard on duty was incredibly rude and arrogant. When I asked to go inside, she bluntly stopped me and said, "Abhi Time nahi huva
​When I politely told her it was already 8:40 PM, she started arguing with immense attitude, saying, "Koi bhi theater me jao, 15 mins pahile hi chodte hai use pahile nhi bahar likha dekh lo."
​Is this how Miraj Cinemas trains its staff to talk to customers? There is a way to communicate rules politely, but her tone was disrespectful and completely uncalled for. Customers pay for a good experience, not to tolerate the tantrums and third-class attitude of your security staff.
​

featured_reviews.name: Deep Rajgor
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

NY Cinemas Mulund is one of the better theatres compared to many others I’ve visited. The best part is the location – just a 2-minute walk from Mulund railway station, which makes it very convenient.

🎬 My Experience:
I’ve watched many films here – Pushpa, Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3, Chandu Champion, Dunki, and more. Every time, the experience has been quite good overall.

🛋️ Seats:
The seats are very comfortable and better than most nearby theatres. Sitting through a 2.5 to 3-hour movie feels easy and relaxed.

❄️ AC (Important Point):
This is the same issue I’ve noticed in almost every theatre nowadays – the AC is not as strong or consistent as before. Back in the 2000–2017 era, theatres used to keep the cooling so high that people carried jackets just to watch movies. In fact, some people even bought tickets only to sleep in the theatre because the AC was so powerful! Now, that unique theatre “chill” experience is gone. The AC here is okay, but not at the superior level it once used to be.

Also, ticket prices have increased a lot. Sometimes, when another theatre is charging ₹130, here it may go up to ₹200. With higher prices, at least the AC should be maintained well.

🔊 Sound & Screen:
The sound quality is balanced with new technology – dialogues are clear, music and effects are impactful without being too loud. The screen size is medium – not too big, not too small – just right for a good movie outing.

👋 Staff & Entry:
The staff are professional, though unlike some theatres (like Miraj), I didn’t notice greetings like “Good Evening” at the entry. Small gestures like that add a nice human touch, but it’s fine.

⏳ Waiting Area:
If you arrive too early, there isn’t much waiting or seating space outside the halls. Better to come on time, as space is limited.

✅ Overall:
A reliable theatre near Mulund station with comfortable seats, decent AC (though not as great as the old days), good sound, and medium-sized screen. Convenient for regular movie-goers like me and definitely better than a lot of nearby options.

featured_reviews.name: Neeta
featured_reviews.review_text: This is my first time at Devgn Cinemas. I had high expectations thinking it was Ajay Devgns cinema chain but the experience is very disappointing. I came here to watch Dhurandar 2 . I paid 350+ for premium seat but the seating was very uncomfortable. At first i thought since the lights are on the screen is blurry and sound is slow. But the projection is bad and a blue light shadow is constantly on the screen in the background when while the movie is on, Colors are faded and maybe the projector is poor so you won't get a cinema experience and sound quality is even worse. From someone coming from a film fraternity they should have worked on all the factors while opening a cinema chain. I think maybe Ajay Devgn should personally come and experience it to understand the issue. People come to a cinema hall for experience but this was a disaster. The movie was not even over and the lights got switched on around 10 mins prior when we asked to switch off they said arre movie almost over hi toh hai. Over all not a great experience here would surely not recommend or come back.

When movie starts some people constantly watch for couples,where they are seated, in front and extreme back seats, and in between movie these people purposely change seats continuously and try sitting next or parallel to the seats where couples are seating. I dont know what is moto, are they trying to extract money from people or try to make the girl feel uncomfortable but this happened many time during movie period. I went with my wife and the same guy tried sitting 2 seats next to my wife and was continuously looking at her. When i asked him what is his seat no. He quickly got up and moved next to another couple sitting on front seats.

The walls and roof were all broken and had big scary holes in them. The waiting lounge outside the halls were a bit better but only a Single fan was available. Food was so damn costly and the taste wasn't even worth it. One Sandwich costs ₹200 and a Small Cheese Popcorn bucket cost us ₹300. We literally wasted ₹500 on food for nothing. Tickets costs ₹180 per person for the Prime seats. Seats were also so uncomfortable. It's actually better if you would book the Recliners to watch the movie peacefully or better if you won't go there at all. Also, there were barely 20 people max who actually watched the movie there. You can see for yourself in my pictures how empty the hall was. For me, this place doesn't match at all compared to it's name. Better go to INOX or some better places for watching movies in the theatres.

The cinema operates comprising approximately with a seating capacity of around 250 to 400 seats.

I was surprised to find that the cinema does not provide any parking facility for visitors. This causes significant inconvenience to patrons and results in traffic congestion in the surrounding area. featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very good experience at PVR ICON Infiniti Andheri (W) Mumbai in Mumbai. It is one of the best places to watch movies with friends and family. The theatre is clean, well-maintained, and has a premium feel. The seating is very comfortable, and the recliner options make the movie experience even better. The screen quality is excellent, and the sound system is powerful, which makes every movie more enjoyable. Many auditoriums here use advanced sound like Dolby Atmos for an immersive experience.  
Infiniti Mall
The staff is polite and helpful, and the entry process is smooth. Online ticket booking is easy, and the theatre usually manages crowds well, even on weekends. The washrooms and waiting area are also neat and hygienic. Snacks like popcorn, cold drinks, and fast food are available inside. The prices are a bit high, but the quality and overall experience are worth it.
The location inside Infiniti Mall is also very convenient, as people can enjoy shopping and food before or after the movie. It is easy to reach by public transport and private vehicle. The atmosphere is safe, friendly, and perfect for entertainment.
Overall, PVR Andheri offers a great movie experience with good comfort, sound, and screen quality. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a premium cinema experience in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Naincy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Overview
Cinépolis is one of the most popular multiplex chains in Mumbai, known for its sleek, modern design and high-end cinematic technology. Whether you are visiting the one in Andheri, Thane, or Navi Mumbai, the vibe is consistently premium. It’s a top-tier choice for movie-goers who prioritize comfort, crystal-clear visuals, and a great atmosphere for a day out with friends or family.
Pros:
Superior Comfort: The seating is well-spaced with excellent legroom. If you opt for the VIP or IMAX screens, the leather recliners are incredibly cozy.
Cutting-Edge Tech: They use advanced laser projection and Dolby Atmos sound systems, making the action feel very immersive.
Variety of Formats: Depending on the location, you can choose from 4DX (moving seats/effects), IMAX, or their luxury "Coffee Tree" service.
Cleanliness: The lobbies and washrooms are generally well-maintained and have a "high-class" feel.
Cons:
Expensive Concessions: Like most premium malls, the popcorn and sodas are quite pricey—sometimes costing more than the movie ticket itself!
Peak Hour Crowds: During big blockbuster releases or weekends, the lobby can get very crowded, leading to long queues at the security check and food counters.
Parking Fees: Since most Cinépolis theaters are inside major malls, you’ll have to pay the standard (and sometimes steep) mall parking rates.

featured_reviews.review_text: Cinepolis Andheri has always been more than just a movie theatre for me. I have been visiting this place for more than a decade, and every single visit carries a different memory attached to it. From watching exciting first day first shows with friends to spending peaceful evenings alone with popcorn and a good film, this place has silently witnessed many phases of my life. The atmosphere, the familiar ticket counters, the glowing posters, and even the smell of freshly made popcorn instantly bring back old emotions whenever I walk inside. No matter how much the city changes, Cinepolis Andheri still feels comfortingly familiar to me. Some places are special because of their beauty, while others become special because of the memories created there. For me, this theatre represents laughter, friendships, excitement, and countless unforgettable moments. Every corner reminds me of a different chapter of my journey. Even today, whenever I visit Cinepolis Andheri, I feel the same happiness and nostalgia that I felt years ago, making it a truly irreplaceable place in my heart. No matter how busy life becomes, returning there always feels like revisiting a comforting piece of my past that still warmly welcomes me home again

featured_reviews.review_text: Maison PVR is a genuine experience of uber luxury and spotless beauty. One of the newest and most beautiful Theatre in town. Sound system, Screen size and interiors of all theatres are different and unique. Highly recommended place to view your latest movies if you want to experience luxury.

featured_reviews.name: Valine Lopes
featured_reviews.review_text:
The theatre should ideally be shut down.
The sound was disastrous, we couldn't even hear the dialogues properly. No subtitles which made it even more difficult to understand what was happening.
The picture quality was pathetic.
The lobby area was way too hot, it gets crowded prior to the movie and is so suffocating and to top of all,the lift was not working either.
The theatre is on the third floor. As a result of which many Senior citizens/ Heart patients had to forfeit their tickets. This is absolutely unacceptable.
The toilets were filthy. No tissues ,the hand soap was black and had a weird smell coming out of it.
Never again I'm I going back and I would never suggest this theatre to anyone.
Pay the same amount and watch a movie at La Reve instead please.
